nameStory: The "pleated" in this moss's name comes from the distinctive way its leaves fold and crease when they dry out, creating tiny accordion-like pleats along the stem. When moisture returns, these pleats unfold like a tiny green fan, giving the moss its characteristic textured appearance that resembles fine fabric.
description: Pleated Foxtail Moss is a small, feathery moss that forms loose, spreading mats on soil and rocks. The individual plants grow in delicate, branching patterns that look like miniature fern fronds, typically reaching only 1-2 inches tall. Its bright to yellow-green color makes it stand out against darker forest backgrounds, and it has a soft, almost silky texture when moist.

idTips.label: Growth Form
idTips.description: Forms loose, feathery mats with irregularly branched stems that spread horizontally before curving upward at the tips, creating a delicate plume-like appearance

idTips.label: Leaves
idTips.description: Tiny oval leaves with pointed tips that overlap like shingles along the stem; when dry, they fold into distinctive pleats, but when moist they spread outward giving a fluffy texture

idTips.label: Color
idTips.description: Bright yellow-green when moist and healthy, becoming duller olive-green when dry; maintains its vibrant color better than many mosses

idTips.label: Texture
idTips.description: Feels soft and slightly springy when moist, like touching a tiny cushion; becomes crispy and brittle when completely dry

idTips.label: Sporophytes
idTips.description: Produces curved, cylindrical capsules on reddish-brown stalks that arch gracefully over the moss like tiny street lamps

idTips.label: Habitat
idTips.description: Prefers disturbed soil, path edges, and rocky outcrops in partial shade; often found where other vegetation is sparse

habitat: Look for Pleated Foxtail Moss along forest paths, on disturbed soil, and rocky outcrops throughout New England's woodlands. It particularly favors spots with partial shade and good drainage, often appearing on banks, trail edges, and areas where the forest canopy lets in dappled sunlight. This moss seems to thrive in places where foot traffic or natural disturbance keeps other plants from taking over.

seasonality.spring: Fresh green growth begins as moisture increases, with the pleated leaves unfurling into their full feathery texture. Sporophyte stalks start developing during late spring.
seasonality.summer: Shows its brightest yellow-green coloration during humid summer days. Sporophyte capsules mature and release spores, often visible as curved brown stalks rising above the moss.
seasonality.fall: Remains vibrant through early fall but begins to show more muted coloration as temperatures drop. Still easily identifiable by its distinctive pleated leaf arrangement.
seasonality.winter: Stays visible under light snow cover, appearing more compressed and olive-colored. The pleated texture becomes more pronounced as the moss enters dormancy.

funFact: This moss can lose up to 95% of its water content and appear completely dead, only to spring back to vibrant life within minutes of receiving moisture – a superpower that allows it to survive in harsh, exposed locations where other plants would perish.
confusionNotes: Most commonly confused with other feather mosses, but the distinctive pleated leaves when dry are the giveaway – other feather mosses curl or twist when dry, but don't form the neat accordion-like pleats that give this species its name.
contextualKnowledge: Despite its name suggesting abundance, Pleated Foxtail Moss appears to be quite uncommon in New England, with very few documented observations. This rarity makes any sighting particularly noteworthy for local naturalists and moss enthusiasts.
compareHints: Unlike its relatives Waterside Feather Moss (which prefers wet areas) and Smooth-stalk Feather-moss (which forms denser mats), Pleated Foxtail Moss has those distinctive pleated leaves and prefers drier, more disturbed habitats. The pleating characteristic is unique among New England's Brachythecium mosses and serves as the most reliable identifying feature.

relatedSpecies.distinction: Unlike its relatives Smooth-stalk and Rough-stalked Feather-moss which can tolerate drier conditions, Waterside Feather Moss is strictly aquatic in its needs.

Among its Brachythecium relatives, Smooth-stalk Feather-moss is the most generalist - while Waterside Feather Moss prefers wet areas and Whitish Feather-moss has a distinctly paler color, this species grows almost anywhere.

Among its feather-moss relatives, Rough-stalked Feather-moss stands out for its bumpy stem texture — Smooth-stalk Feather-moss feels smooth, Waterside Feather-moss prefers wet areas, and Whitish Feather-moss has a distinctly paler, more silvery appearance.
Compared to its Brachythecium relatives like Rough-stalked and Smooth-stalk Feather-moss, Whitish Feather-moss is distinctly paler in color and typically smaller in overall size.
